index 0000000..09e7b04
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/mistune/renderers/html.py
@@ -0,0 +1,215 @@
+import re
+from typing import Any, ClassVar, Dict, Iterable, Literal, Mapping, Optional, Tuple, Union
+from urllib.parse import unquote
+
+from ..core import BaseRenderer, BlockState
+from ..util import escape as escape_text
+from ..util import safe_entity, striptags
+
+
+class HTMLRenderer(BaseRenderer):
+    """A renderer for converting Markdown to HTML."""
+
+    _escape: bool
+    _allow_harmful_protocols: Optional[Union[bool, Iterable[str]]]
+    NAME: ClassVar[Literal["html"]] = "html"
+    SAFE_PROTOCOLS: ClassVar[Tuple[str, ...]] = (
+        "http:",
+        "https:",
+        "mailto:",
+        "tel:",
+        "ftp:",
+        "ftps:",
+        "irc:",
+        "ircs:",
+    )
+    GOOD_DATA_PROTOCOLS: ClassVar[Tuple[str, ...]] = (
+        "data:image/gif;",
+        "data:image/png;",
+        "data:image/jpeg;",
+        "data:image/webp;",
+    )
+    _attribute_name_re = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*$")
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        escape: bool = True,
+        allow_harmful_protocols: Optional[Union[bool, Iterable[str]]] = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        super(HTMLRenderer, self).__init__()
+        self._allow_harmful_protocols = allow_harmful_protocols
+        self._escape = escape
+
+    @property
+    def escape_enabled(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether raw HTML nodes are escaped."""
+        return self._escape
+
+    @escape_enabled.setter
+    def escape_enabled(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
+        self._escape = enabled
+
+    def escape_raw(self, value: str) -> str:
+        """Escape raw HTML when raw HTML output is disabled."""
+        if self.escape_enabled:
+            return escape_text(value)
+        return value
+
+    def escape_attribute(self, value: object) -> str:
+        """Escape a value for use in a generated HTML attribute."""
+        return safe_entity(str(value))
+
+    def render_attrs(self, attrs: Mapping[str, object]) -> str:
+        """Render generated HTML attributes with escaped values."""
+        rendered = []
+        for name, value in attrs.items():
+            if not self._attribute_name_re.fullmatch(name):
+                raise ValueError("invalid HTML attribute name: " + name)
+            if value is None or value is False:
+                continue
+            if value is True:
+                rendered.append(" " + name)
+            else:
+                rendered.append(' ' + name + '="' + self.escape_attribute(value) + '"')
+        return "".join(rendered)
+
+    def sanitize_url(self, url: str) -> str:
+        """Return a URL allowed by this renderer's protocol policy."""
+        allow_harmful_protocols = self._allow_harmful_protocols
+        if allow_harmful_protocols is True:
+            return url
+
+        normalized_url = _unquote_url(url).lower().lstrip()
+        if allow_harmful_protocols and normalized_url.startswith(tuple(allow_harmful_protocols)):
+            return url
+
+        if _is_safe_url(normalized_url, self.SAFE_PROTOCOLS, self.GOOD_DATA_PROTOCOLS):
+            return url
+        return "#harmful-link"
+
+    def render_token(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        # backward compitable with v2
+        func = self._get_method(token["type"])
+        attrs = token.get("attrs")
+
+        if "raw" in token:
+            text = token["raw"]
+        elif "children" in token:
+            text = self.render_tokens(token["children"], state)
+        else:
+            if attrs:
+                return func(**attrs)
+            else:
+                return func()
+        if attrs:
+            return func(text, **attrs)
+        else:
+            return func(text)
+
+    def safe_url(self, url: str) -> str:
+        """Ensure the given URL is safe. This method is used for rendering
+        links, images, and etc.
+        """
+        return self.escape_attribute(self.sanitize_url(url))
+
+    def text(self, text: str) -> str:
+        if self.escape_enabled:
+            return escape_text(text)
+        return safe_entity(text)
+
+    def emphasis(self, text: str) -> str:
+        return "<em>" + text + "</em>"
+
+    def strong(self, text: str) -> str:
+        return "<strong>" + text + "</strong>"
+
+    def link(self, text: str, url: str, title: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
+        attrs: Dict[str, object] = {"href": self.sanitize_url(url)}
+        if title:
+            attrs["title"] = title
+        return "<a" + self.render_attrs(attrs) + ">" + text + "</a>"
+
+    def image(self, text: str, url: str, title: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
+        alt = striptags(text)
+        attrs: Dict[str, object] = {"src": self.sanitize_url(url), "alt": alt}
+        if title:
+            attrs["title"] = title
+        return "<img" + self.render_attrs(attrs) + " />"
+
+    def codespan(self, text: str) -> str:
+        return "<code>" + escape_text(text) + "</code>"
+
+    def linebreak(self) -> str:
+        return "<br />\n"
+
+    def softbreak(self) -> str:
+        return "\n"
+
+    def inline_html(self, html: str) -> str:
+        return self.escape_raw(html)
+
+    def paragraph(self, text: str) -> str:
+        return "<p>" + text + "</p>\n"
+
+    def heading(self, text: str, level: int, **attrs: Any) -> str:
+        tag = "h" + str(level)
+        _id = attrs.get("id")
+        rendered_attrs = self.render_attrs({"id": _id}) if _id else ""
+        return "<" + tag + rendered_attrs + ">" + text + "</" + tag + ">\n"
+
+    def blank_line(self) -> str:
+        return ""
+
+    def thematic_break(self) -> str:
+        return "<hr />\n"
+
+    def block_text(self, text: str) -> str:
+        return text
+
+    def block_code(self, code: str, info: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
+        attrs: Dict[str, object] = {}
+        if info is not None:
+            info = safe_entity(info.strip())
+        if info:
+            lang = info.split(None, 1)[0]
+            attrs["class"] = "language-" + lang
+        return "<pre><code" + self.render_attrs(attrs) + ">" + escape_text(code) + "</code></pre>\n"
+
+    def block_quote(self, text: str) -> str:
+        return "<blockquote>\n" + text + "</blockquote>\n"
+
+    def block_html(self, html: str) -> str:
+        if self.escape_enabled:
+            return "<p>" + self.escape_raw(html.strip()) + "</p>\n"
+        return html + "\n"
+
+    def block_error(self, text: str) -> str:
+        return '<div class="error"><pre>' + escape_text(text) + "</pre></div>\n"
+
+    def list(self, text: str, ordered: bool, **attrs: Any) -> str:
+        if ordered:
+            start = attrs.get("start")
+            return "<ol" + self.render_attrs({"start": start}) + ">\n" + text + "</ol>\n"
+        return "<ul>\n" + text + "</ul>\n"
+
+    def list_item(self, text: str) -> str:
+        return "<li>" + text + "</li>\n"
+
+
+def _unquote_url(url: str) -> str:
+    for _ in range(3):
+        decoded = unquote(url)
+        if decoded == url:
+            break
+        url = decoded
+    return url
+
+
+def _is_safe_url(url: str, safe_protocols: Tuple[str, ...], good_data_protocols: Tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
+    if url.startswith(safe_protocols):
+        return True
+    if url.startswith(good_data_protocols):
+        return True
+    if url.startswith(("/", "#", "?")):
+        return True
+    return ":" not in url.split("/", 1)[0]
diff --git a/src/mistune/renderers/markdown.py b/src/mistune/renderers/markdown.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cc65262
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/mistune/renderers/markdown.py
@@ -0,0 +1,310 @@
+import re
+from textwrap import indent
+from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, cast
+
+from ..core import BaseRenderer, BlockState
+from ..util import strip_end
+from ._list import render_list, render_list_item
+
+fenced_re = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}([`~]+)", re.M)
+_backtick_run_re = re.compile(r"`+")
+_literal_inline_markers_re = re.compile(r"&(?:#[0-9]+|#[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+|[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]+);|([\\`<!&])")
+
+#: leading markers that would be parsed as a new block (list, heading, block
+#: quote) if they appear unescaped at the start of a line.
+_block_prefix_re = re.compile(r"^(\s*)(>|[-+*]|#{1,6}|\d{1,9}[.)])(\s|$)")
+
+
+class MarkdownRenderer(BaseRenderer):
+    """A renderer to re-format Markdown text."""
+
+    NAME = "markdown"
+
+    def __call__(self, tokens: Iterable[Dict[str, Any]], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        tokens = list(tokens)
+        leading = ""
+        i = 0
+        while i < len(tokens) and tokens[i]["type"] == "blank_line" and "newlines" in tokens[i]:
+            leading += "\n" * tokens[i]["newlines"]
+            i += 1
+        out = self.render_tokens(tokens[i:], state)
+        # special handle for line breaks
+        out += "\n\n".join(self.render_referrences(state)) + "\n"
+        return strip_end(leading + out)
+
+    def render_referrences(self, state: BlockState) -> Iterable[str]:
+        ref_links = state.env["ref_links"]
+        for key in ref_links:
+            attrs = ref_links[key]
+            # An empty destination must be explicit in a reference definition.
+            url = attrs["url"] or "<>"
+            text = "[" + attrs["label"] + "]: " + url
+            title = attrs.get("title")
+            if title:
+                text += ' "' + _escape_title(title) + '"'
+            yield text
+
+    def render_children(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        children = token["children"]
+        return self.render_tokens(children, state)
+
+    def text(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        raw = cast(str, token["raw"])
+        # a text token that is made up entirely of "*"/"_" is a literal
+        # emphasis delimiter -- either an escaped marker from the source
+        # (``\*``) or an unmatched leftover -- so every character must stay
+        # escaped, or it would re-parse as emphasis on the round-trip. Prose
+        # punctuation such as ``2 * 3`` or ``snake_case`` arrives mixed with
+        # other characters and is left untouched.
+        if raw and all(c in "*_" for c in raw):
+            return "".join("\\" + c for c in raw)
+        # Keep literal escapes, code delimiters, image introducers, HTML
+        # delimiters and entity prefixes from becoming markup on re-parse.
+        # Complete entity references already in this token keep their meaning;
+        # escaped ampersands arrive in a separate text token.
+        return _literal_inline_markers_re.sub(lambda m: "\\" + m[1] if m[1] else m[0], raw)
+
+    def emphasis(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "*" + self.render_children(token, state) + "*"
+
+    def strong(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "**" + self.render_children(token, state) + "**"
+
+    # Inline formatting plugins (strikethrough, mark, insert)
+    def strikethrough(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "~~" + self.render_children(token, state) + "~~"
+
+    def mark(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "==" + self.render_children(token, state) + "=="
+
+    def insert(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "^^" + self.render_children(token, state) + "^^"
+
+    def link(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        label = cast(str, token.get("label"))
+        text = self.render_children(token, state)
+        out = "[" + text + "]"
+        if label:
+            return out + "[" + label + "]"
+
+        attrs = token["attrs"]
+        url: str = attrs["url"]
+        title = attrs.get("title")
+        if token["type"] == "link" and text == url and not title:
+            return "<" + text + ">"
+        elif token["type"] == "link" and "mailto:" + text == url and not title:
+            return "<" + text + ">"
+
+        out += "("
+        if "(" in url or ")" in url:
+            out += "<" + url + ">"
+        else:
+            out += url
+        if title:
+            out += ' "' + _escape_title(title) + '"'
+        return out + ")"
+
+    def image(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "!" + self.link(token, state)
+
+    def codespan(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        code = cast(str, token["raw"])
+        # The delimiter must be a run of backticks longer than any backtick run
+        # inside the content, otherwise the content would close the span early.
+        longest = max((len(run) for run in _backtick_run_re.findall(code)), default=0)
+        fence = "`" * (longest + 1)
+        # Padding separates edge backticks from the delimiter and protects
+        # meaningful spaces at both ends from the parser's space normalization.
+        # All-space content is exempt from that normalization.
+        if (
+            code.startswith("`")
+            or code.endswith("`")
+            or (code.startswith(" ") and code.endswith(" ") and code.strip(" "))
+        ):
+            return fence + " " + code + " " + fence
+        return fence + code + fence
+
+    def linebreak(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "  \n"
+
+    def softbreak(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "\n"
+
+    def blank_line(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return ""
+
+    def inline_html(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return cast(str, token["raw"])
+
+    def paragraph(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        text = self.render_children(token, state)
+        return _escape_block_prefix(text) + "\n\n"
+
+    def heading(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        level = cast(int, token["attrs"]["level"])
+        text = self.render_children(token, state)
+        # An ATX heading ("# ...") occupies a single line, so a heading whose
+        # rendered text spans several lines -- a multi-line setext heading --
+        # must be re-emitted in setext form. As ATX the continuation lines
+        # would fall out of the heading and become a paragraph on a re-parse.
+        # Only levels 1 and 2 reach this branch, since an ATX heading never
+        # contains a line break.
+        if "\n" in text and level in (1, 2):
+            underline = "=" if level == 1 else "-"
+            return text + "\n" + underline * 3 + "\n\n"
+        marker = "#" * level
+        text = re.sub(r"(^|[ \t])(#+)$", r"\1\\\2", text)
+        return marker + " " + text + "\n\n"
+
+    def thematic_break(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "***\n\n"
+
+    def block_text(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return _escape_block_prefix(self.render_children(token, state)) + "\n"
+
+    def block_code(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        attrs = token.get("attrs", {})
+        info = cast(str, attrs.get("info", ""))
+        code = cast(str, token["raw"])
+        if code and code[-1] != "\n":
+            code += "\n"
+
+        marker = token.get("marker")
+        if not marker:
+            marker = _get_fenced_marker(code)
+        marker2 = cast(str, marker)
+        return marker2 + info + "\n" + code + marker2 + "\n\n"
+
+    def block_quote(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        # strip the children's trailing blank lines first so the quote marker is
+        # not added to a dangling empty line; stripping it back off afterwards
+        # would also eat a ">" that ends the content (an autolink or HTML tag).
+        text = self.render_children(token, state).rstrip("\n")
+        text = indent(text, "> ", lambda _: True)
+        return text + "\n\n"
+
+    def block_html(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return cast(str, token["raw"]) + "\n\n"
+
+    def block_error(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return ""
+
+    def list(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return render_list(self, token, state)
+
+    def list_item(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return render_list_item(self, token, state)
+
+    def task_list_item(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        checked = token.get("attrs", {}).get("checked")
+        marker = "[x] " if checked else "[ ] "
+        return render_list_item(self, token, state, marker)
+
+    def table(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        children = token.get("children", [])
+        if not children:
+            return "\n"
+
+        head = children[0]
+        body = children[1] if len(children) > 1 else None
+        head_cells = head.get("children", [])
+        align = [_table_cell_align(cell) for cell in head_cells]
+        lines = [
+            _render_table_row(self, head_cells, state),
+            _render_table_delimiter(align),
+        ]
+        if body:
+            for row in body.get("children", []):
+                lines.append(_render_table_row(self, row.get("children", []), state))
+        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"
+
+    def table_head(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        cells = token.get("children", [])
+        return (
+            _render_table_row(self, cells, state)
+            + "\n"
+            + _render_table_delimiter([_table_cell_align(c) for c in cells])
+        )
+
+    def table_body(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "\n".join(self.render_token(row, state).rstrip("\n") for row in token.get("children", []))
+
+    def table_row(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return _render_table_row(self, token.get("children", []), state) + "\n"
+
+    def table_cell(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return _render_table_cell(self, token, state)
+
+
+def _escape_title(title: str) -> str:
+    """Escape a link/image title for emission inside double quotes. The closing
+    quote would otherwise end the title early on a re-parse; a backslash is
+    escaped first so it can't combine with the following character."""
+    return title.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
+
+
+def _escape_block_prefix(text: str) -> str:
+    """Backslash-escape a leading block marker on each line so that literal
+    text is not re-parsed as a list, heading or block quote."""
+    return "\n".join(_escape_line_prefix(line) for line in text.split("\n"))
+
+
+def _escape_line_prefix(line: str) -> str:
+    m = _block_prefix_re.match(line)
+    if not m:
+        return line
+    indent_, marker = m.group(1), m.group(2)
+    return indent_ + marker[:-1] + "\\" + marker[-1] + line[m.end(2) :]
+
+
+def _get_fenced_marker(code: str) -> str:
+    found = fenced_re.findall(code)
+    if not found:
+        return "```"
+
+    ticks = []  # `
+    waves = []  # ~
+    for s in found:
+        if s[0] == "`":
+            ticks.append(len(s))
+        else:
+            waves.append(len(s))
+
+    if not ticks:
+        return "```"
+
+    if not waves:
+        return "~~~"
+    return "`" * (max(ticks) + 1)
+
+
+def _render_table_row(renderer: MarkdownRenderer, cells: Iterable[Dict[str, Any]], state: BlockState) -> str:
+    return "| " + " | ".join(_render_table_cell(renderer, cell, state) for cell in cells) + " |"
+
+
+def _render_table_delimiter(aligns: Iterable[Any]) -> str:
+    cells = []
+    for align in aligns:
+        if align == "left":
+            cells.append(":---")
+        elif align == "center":
+            cells.append(":---:")
+        elif align == "right":
+            cells.append("---:")
+        else:
+            cells.append("---")
+    return "| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |"
+
+
+def _render_table_cell(renderer: MarkdownRenderer, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+    if "children" in token:
+        text = renderer.render_children(token, state)
+    else:
+        text = cast(str, token.get("raw", ""))
+    # Code spans can already contain escaped pipes; keep an odd escape count.
+    text = re.sub(r"\\.|[|]", lambda m: r"\|" if m[0] == "|" else m[0], text)
+    return text.replace("\n", " ").strip()
+
+
+def _table_cell_align(token: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
+    return token.get("attrs", {}).get("align")

+from textwrap import indent
+from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, cast
+
+from ..core import BaseRenderer, BlockState
+from ..util import strip_end
+from ._list import render_list, render_list_item
+
+
+class RSTRenderer(BaseRenderer):
+    """A renderer for converting Markdown to ReST."""
+
+    NAME = "rst"
+
+    #: marker symbols for heading
+    HEADING_MARKERS = {
+        1: "=",
+        2: "-",
+        3: "~",
+        4: "^",
+        5: '"',
+        6: "'",
+    }
+    INLINE_IMAGE_PREFIX = "img-"
+
+    def iter_tokens(self, tokens: Iterable[Dict[str, Any]], state: BlockState) -> Iterable[str]:
+        prev = None
+        for tok in tokens:
+            # ignore blank line
+            if tok["type"] == "blank_line":
+                continue
+            tok["prev"] = prev
+            prev = tok
+            yield self.render_token(tok, state)
+
+    def __call__(self, tokens: Iterable[Dict[str, Any]], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        state.env["inline_images"] = []
+        out = self.render_tokens(tokens, state)
+        # special handle for line breaks
+        out += "\n\n".join(self.render_referrences(state)) + "\n"
+        return strip_end(out)
+
+    def render_referrences(self, state: BlockState) -> Iterable[str]:
+        images = state.env["inline_images"]
+        for index, token in enumerate(images):
+            attrs = token["attrs"]
+            alt = self.render_children(token, state)
+            ident = self.INLINE_IMAGE_PREFIX + str(index)
+            yield ".. |" + ident + "| image:: " + attrs["url"] + "\n   :alt: " + alt
+
+    def render_children(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        children = token["children"]
+        return self.render_tokens(children, state)
+
+    def text(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        text = cast(str, token["raw"])
+        return text.replace("|", r"\|")
+
+    def emphasis(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "*" + self.render_children(token, state) + "*"
+
+    def strong(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "**" + self.render_children(token, state) + "**"
+
+    def link(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        attrs = token["attrs"]
+        text = self.render_children(token, state)
+        return "`" + text + " <" + cast(str, attrs["url"]) + ">`__"
+
+    def image(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        refs: List[Dict[str, Any]] = state.env["inline_images"]
+        index = len(refs)
+        refs.append(token)
+        return "|" + self.INLINE_IMAGE_PREFIX + str(index) + "|"
+
+    def codespan(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "``" + cast(str, token["raw"]) + "``"
+
+    def linebreak(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "<linebreak>"
+
+    def softbreak(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return " "
+
+    def inline_html(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        # rst does not support inline html
+        return ""
+
+    def paragraph(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        children = token["children"]
+        if len(children) == 1 and children[0]["type"] == "image":
+            image = children[0]
+            attrs = image["attrs"]
+            title = cast(str, attrs.get("title"))
+            alt = self.render_children(image, state)
+            text = ".. figure:: " + cast(str, attrs["url"])
+            if title:
+                text += "\n   :alt: " + title
+            text += "\n\n" + indent(alt, "   ")
+        else:
+            text = self.render_tokens(children, state)
+            lines = text.split("<linebreak>")
+            if len(lines) > 1:
+                text = "\n".join("| " + line for line in lines)
+        return text + "\n\n"
+
+    def heading(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        attrs = token["attrs"]
+        text = self.render_children(token, state)
+        marker = self.HEADING_MARKERS[attrs["level"]]
+        return text + "\n" + marker * len(text) + "\n\n"
+
+    def thematic_break(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return "--------------\n\n"
+
+    def block_text(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        text = self.render_children(token, state)
+        lines = text.split("<linebreak>")
+        if len(lines) > 1:
+            text = "\n".join("| " + line for line in lines)
+        return text + "\n"
+
+    def block_code(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        attrs = token.get("attrs", {})
+        info = cast(str, attrs.get("info"))
+        code = indent(cast(str, token["raw"]), "   ")
+        if info:
+            lang = info.split()[0]
+            return ".. code:: " + lang + "\n\n" + code + "\n"
+        else:
+            return "::\n\n" + code + "\n\n"
+
+    def block_quote(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        text = indent(self.render_children(token, state), "   ")
+        prev = token.get("prev")
+        ignore_blocks = (
+            "paragraph",
+            "block_text",
+            "thematic_break",
+            "linebreak",
+            "heading",
+        )
+        if prev and prev["type"] not in ignore_blocks:
+            text = "..\n\n" + text
+        return text
+
+    def block_html(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        raw = token["raw"]
+        return ".. raw:: html\n\n" + indent(raw, "   ") + "\n\n"
+
+    def block_error(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return ""
+
+    def list(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return render_list(self, token, state)
+
+    def list_item(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        return render_list_item(self, token, state)
+
+    def task_list_item(self, token: Dict[str, Any], state: BlockState) -> str:
+        checked = token.get("attrs", {}).get("checked")
+        marker = "[x] " if checked else "[ ] "
+        return render_list_item(self, token, state, marker)

+import re
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Set, Tuple
+
+from .core import BlockState
+from .util import escape, striptags
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from .markdown import Markdown
+
+_HTML_ID_RE = re.compile(r"""\bid\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')""", re.I)
+
+
+def add_toc_hook(
+    md: "Markdown",
+    min_level: int = 1,
+    max_level: int = 3,
+    heading_id: Optional[Callable[[Dict[str, Any], int], str]] = None,
+) -> None:
+    """Add a hook to save toc items into ``state.env``. This is
+    usually helpful for doc generator::
+
+        import mistune
+        from mistune.toc import add_toc_hook, render_toc_ul
+
+        md = mistune.create_markdown(...)
+        add_toc_hook(md)
+
+        html, state = md.parse(text)
+        toc_items = state.env['toc_items']
+        toc_html = render_toc_ul(toc_items)
+
+    :param md: Markdown instance
+    :param min_level: min heading level
+    :param max_level: max heading level
+    :param heading_id: a function to generate heading_id
+    """
+    if heading_id is None:
+        auto_heading_id = True
+
+        def heading_id(token: Dict[str, Any], index: int) -> str:
+            return "toc_" + str(index + 1)
+
+    else:
+        auto_heading_id = False
+
+    def toc_hook(md: "Markdown", state: "BlockState") -> None:
+        headings = []
+
+        for tok in state.tokens:
+            if tok["type"] == "heading":
+                level = tok["attrs"]["level"]
+                if min_level <= level <= max_level:
+                    headings.append(tok)
+
+        id_allocator = _HeadingIdAllocator(state, headings)
+        toc_items = []
+        for i, tok in enumerate(headings):
+            if not tok["attrs"].get("id"):
+                value = heading_id(tok, i)
+                id_allocator.assign(tok, value, ensure_unique=auto_heading_id)
+            toc_items.append(normalize_toc_item(md, tok, parent=state))
+
+        # save items into state
+        state.env["toc_items"] = toc_items
+
+    md.before_render_hooks.append(toc_hook)
+
+
+class _HeadingIdAllocator:
+    def __init__(self, state: "BlockState", headings: Iterable[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
+        self.used_ids: Set[str] = {m.group(1) or m.group(2) for m in _HTML_ID_RE.finditer(state.src)}
+        for token in headings:
+            value = token.get("attrs", {}).get("id")
+            if value:
+                self.used_ids.add(value)
+
+    def assign(self, token: Dict[str, Any], value: str, ensure_unique: bool = True) -> str:
+        if ensure_unique:
+            value = self._unique(value)
+        self.used_ids.add(value)
+        token["attrs"]["id"] = value
+        return value
+
+    def _unique(self, value: str) -> str:
+        if value not in self.used_ids:
+            return value
+
+        index = 1
+        while value + "_" + str(index) in self.used_ids:
+            index += 1
+        return value + "_" + str(index)
+
+
+def normalize_toc_item(md: "Markdown", token: Dict[str, Any], parent: Optional[Any] = None) -> Tuple[int, str, str]:
+    text = token["text"]
+    tokens = md.inline(text, parent.env if parent else {})
+    assert md.renderer is not None
+    html = md.renderer(tokens, BlockState())
+    text = striptags(html)
+    attrs = token["attrs"]
+    return attrs["level"], attrs["id"], text
+
+
+def render_toc_ul(toc: Iterable[Tuple[int, str, str]]) -> str:
+    """Render a <ul> table of content HTML. The param "toc" should
+    be formatted into this structure::
+
+        [
+          (level, id, text),
+        ]
+
+    For example::
+
+        [
+          (1, 'toc-intro', 'Introduction'),
+          (2, 'toc-install', 'Install'),
+          (2, 'toc-upgrade', 'Upgrade'),
+          (1, 'toc-license', 'License'),
+        ]
+    """
+    if not toc:
+        return ""
+
+    s = ""
+    levels: List[int] = []
+    for level, k, text in toc:
+        item = '<a href="#{}">{}</a>'.format(escape(k), text)
+        if not levels:
+            s += "<li>" + item
+            levels.append(level)
+        elif level == levels[-1]:
+            s += "</li>\n<li>" + item
+        elif level > levels[-1]:
+            s += "\n<ul>\n<li>" + item
+            levels.append(level)
+        else:
+            levels.pop()
+            while levels:
+                last_level = levels.pop()
+                if level == last_level:
+                    s += "</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>" + item
+                    levels.append(level)
+                    break
+                elif level > last_level:
+                    s += "</li>\n<li>" + item
+                    levels.append(last_level)
+                    levels.append(level)
+                    break
+                else:
+                    s += "</li>\n</ul>\n"
+            else:
+                levels.append(level)
+                s += "</li>\n<li>" + item
+
+    while len(levels) > 1:
+        s += "</li>\n</ul>\n"
+        levels.pop()
+
+    if not s:
+        return ""
+    return "<ul>\n" + s + "</li>\n</ul>\n"

+import html
+import re
+from typing import Callable, Match, cast
+from urllib.parse import quote
+
+_expand_tab_re = re.compile(r"^( {0,3})\t", flags=re.M)
+_replace_charref = cast(Callable[[Match[str]], str], getattr(html, "_replace_charref"))
+
+
+def expand_leading_tab(text: str, width: int = 4) -> str:
+    def repl(m: Match[str]) -> str:
+        s = m.group(1)
+        return s + " " * (width - len(s))
+
+    return _expand_tab_re.sub(repl, text)
+
+
+def expand_tab(text: str, space: str = "    ") -> str:
+    repl = r"\1" + space
+    return _expand_tab_re.sub(repl, text)
+
+
+def escape(s: str, quote: bool = True) -> str:
+    """Escape characters of ``&<>``. If quote=True, ``"`` will be
+    converted to ``"e;``."""
+    s = s.replace("&", "&")
+    s = s.replace("<", "<")
+    s = s.replace(">", ">")
+    if quote:
+        s = s.replace('"', """)
+    return s
+
+
+def escape_url(link: str) -> str:
+    """Escape URL for safety."""
+    safe = (
+        ":/?#@"  # gen-delims - '[]' (rfc3986)
+        "!$&()*+,;="  # sub-delims - "'" (rfc3986)
+        "%"  # leave already-encoded octets alone
+    )
+    return quote(unescape(link), safe=safe)
+
+
+def safe_entity(s: str) -> str:
+    """Escape characters for safety."""
+    return escape(unescape(s))
+
+
+def unikey(s: str) -> str:
+    """Generate a unique key for links and footnotes."""
+    key = " ".join(s.split()).strip()
+    return key.lower().upper()
+
+
+_charref_re = re.compile(
+    r"&(#[0-9]{1,7};"
+    r"|#[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+;"
+    r"|[^\t\n\f <&#;]{1,32};)"
+)
+
+
+def unescape(s: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Copy from `html.unescape`, but `_charref` is different. CommonMark
+    does not accept entity references without a trailing semicolon
+    """
+    if "&" not in s:
+        return s
+    return _charref_re.sub(_replace_charref, s)
+
+
+_striptags_re = re.compile(r"(<!--.*?-->|<[^>]*>)")
+_strip_image_re = re.compile(r"<img\b[^>]*\balt=(\"([^\"]*)\"|'([^']*)')[^>]*>")
+
+
+def striptags(s: str) -> str:
+    s = _strip_image_re.sub(lambda m: m.group(2) or m.group(3) or "", s)
+    return _striptags_re.sub("", s)
+
+
+def strip_end(src: str) -> str:
+    r"""Strip trailing whitespace after the final line break.
+
+    This used to be implemented as ``re.sub(r"\n\s+$", "\n", src)``.
+    For a long run of blank lines followed by a non-whitespace continuation,
+    the regex retries ``\s+`` from every preceding newline and becomes
+    quadratic.  Scanning the suffix once keeps the same behavior in linear
+    time.
+    """
+    end = len(src)
+    while end and src[end - 1].isspace():
+        end -= 1
+
+    newline = src.find("\n", end)
+    if newline >= 0:
+        return src[:newline] + "\n"
+    return src

+import re
+from abc import abstractmethod
+from unittest import TestCase
+
+from tests import fixtures
+
+
+class BaseTestCase(TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def load_fixtures(cls, case_file: str) -> None:
+        def attach_case(n: str, text: str, html: str) -> None:
+            def method(self: "BaseTestCase") -> None:
+                self.assert_case(n, text, html)
+
+            name = "test_{}".format(n)
+            method.__name__ = name
+            method.__doc__ = "Run fixture {} - {}".format(case_file, n)
+            setattr(cls, name, method)
+
+        for n, text, html in fixtures.load_examples(case_file):
+            if cls.ignore_case(n):
+                continue
+            attach_case(n, text, html)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def ignore_case(cls, name: str) -> bool:
+        return False
+
+    @abstractmethod
+    def parse(self, text: str) -> str: ...
+
+    def assert_case(self, name: str, text: str, html: str) -> None:
+        result = self.parse(text)
+        self.assertEqual(result, html)
+
+
+def normalize_html(html: str) -> str:
+    html = re.sub(r">\n+", ">", html)
+    html = re.sub(r"\n+<", "<", html)
+    return html.strip()

+import json
+import os
+import re
+from typing import Any, Iterable, Tuple
+
+ROOT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__))
+
+EXAMPLE_PATTERN = re.compile(
+    r"^`{32} example\n([\s\S]*?)"
+    r"^\.\n([\s\S]*?)"
+    r"^`{32}$|^#{1,6} *(.*)$",
+    flags=re.M,
+)
+
+
+def load_ast(filename: str) -> Any:
+    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "ast", filename), encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        return json.load(f)
+
+
+def load_json(filename: str) -> Any:
+    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, filename), encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        return json.load(f)
+
+
+def load_examples(filename: str) -> Iterable[Tuple[str, str, str]]:
+    if filename.endswith(".json"):
+        data = load_json(filename)
+        for item in data:
+            section = item["section"].lower().replace(" ", "_")
+            n = "%s_%03d" % (section, item["example"])
+            yield n, item["markdown"], item["html"]
+    else:
+        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, filename), "rb") as f:
+            content = f.read()
+            s = content.decode("utf-8")
+            yield from parse_examples(s)
+
+
+def parse_examples(text: str) -> Iterable[Tuple[str, str, str]]:
+    data = EXAMPLE_PATTERN.findall(text)
+
+    section = None
+    count = 0
+    for md, html, title in data:
+        if title:
+            count = 0
+            section = title.lower().replace(" ", "_")
+
+        if md and html:
+            count += 1
+            n = "%s_%03d" % (section, count)
+            md = md.replace("\u2192", "\t")
+            html = html.replace("\u2192", "\t")
+            yield n, md, html

+Historical CommonMark edge cases.
+
+
+## Links
+
+Autolinks in link text stay literal.
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+[<https://example.com>](/foo)
+.
+<p><a href="/foo"><https://example.com></a></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+[<name@example.com>](/foo)
+.
+<p><a href="/foo"><name@example.com></a></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+[[foo][]][bar]
+
+[foo]: /foo
+[bar]: /bar
+.
+<p>[<a href="/foo">foo</a>]<a href="/bar">bar</a></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+The label of a full reference image is not a link of its own.
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+[![moon][img]](/uri)
+
+[img]: moon.jpg
+.
+<p><a href="/uri"><img src="moon.jpg" alt="moon" /></a></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+[![moon][img]][ref]
+
+[img]: moon.jpg
+[ref]: /uri
+.
+<p><a href="/uri"><img src="moon.jpg" alt="moon" /></a></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+## Emphasis
+
+CommonMark delimiter handling is the default.
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+*_em_* __**strong**__ ______m______
+.
+<p><em><em>em</em></em> <strong><strong>strong</strong></strong> <strong><strong><strong>m</strong></strong></strong></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+*a **b c* d**
+.
+<p><em>a <em><em>b c</em> d</em></em></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+*a **b c* d**
+.
+<p><em>a <em><em>b c</em> d</em></em></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+*a **b c* d
+.
+<p>*a *<em>b c</em> d</p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+The multiple-of-3 rule uses the original delimiter run length, so the
+remainder of a partially consumed run can still match a later delimiter.
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+*a***a*
+.
+<p><em>a</em>*<em>a</em></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+*foo***bar*
+.
+<p><em>foo</em>*<em>bar</em></p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+
+## Lists
+
+An empty list item has no paragraph, so an unindented line after it
+is not a lazy continuation line.
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+-
+foo
+.
+<ul>
+<li></li>
+</ul>
+<p>foo</p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+- a
+-
+b
+.
+<ul>
+<li>a</li>
+<li></li>
+</ul>
+<p>b</p>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+> 1.
+> foo
+.
+<blockquote>
+<ol>
+<li></li>
+</ol>
+<p>foo</p>
+</blockquote>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+
+## Max depth
+
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+> > > > > > > > b
+.
+<blockquote>
+<blockquote>
+<blockquote>
+<blockquote>
+<blockquote>
+<blockquote>
+<blockquote>
+<blockquote>
+<p>b</p>
+</blockquote>
+</blockquote>
+</blockquote>
+</blockquote>
+</blockquote>
+</blockquote>
+</blockquote>
+</blockquote>
+````````````````````````````````
+
+
+```````````````````````````````` example
+- a
+  - b
+    - c
+      - d
+        - e
+          - f
+            - g
+              - h
+.
+<ul>
+<li>a<ul>
+<li>b<ul>
+<li>c<ul>
+<li>d<ul>
+<li>e<ul>
+<li>f<ul>
+<li>g<ul>
+<li>h</li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+</li>
+</ul>
+````````````````````````````````

+```````````````````````````````` example

+import statistics
+import time
+from typing import Callable, Tuple, TypeVar
+from unittest import TestCase
+
+T = TypeVar("T")
+
+
+def assert_near_linear(
+    test_case: TestCase,
+    operation: Callable[[int], T],
+    small_size: int,
+    large_size: int,
+    *,
+    max_growth: float = 3.5,
+    noise_seconds: float = 0.02,
+    warmup_size: int = 200,
+) -> Tuple[T, T]:
+    """Assert that doubling adversarial input has bounded time growth."""
+    if small_size < 1 or large_size <= small_size:
+        raise ValueError("sizes must be positive and increasing")
+
+    operation(warmup_size)
+    small_result, small_elapsed = _measure(operation, small_size)
+    large_result, large_elapsed = _measure(operation, large_size)
+    test_case.assertLess(
+        large_elapsed,
+        small_elapsed * max_growth + noise_seconds,
+        f"time growth {large_elapsed / max(small_elapsed, 1e-12):.2f}x exceeded {max_growth:.2f}x",
+    )
+    return small_result, large_result
+
+
+def _measure(operation: Callable[[int], T], size: int) -> Tuple[T, float]:
+    timings = []
+    result = operation(size)
+    for _ in range(3):
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        result = operation(size)
+        timings.append(time.perf_counter() - started)
+    return result, statistics.median(timings)

+def inline_depth(tokens):
+    maximum = 0
+    stack = [(token, 0) for token in tokens]
+    while stack:
+        token, depth = stack.pop()
+        if "children" in token:
+            depth += 1
+            maximum = max(maximum, depth)
+            stack.extend((child, depth) for child in token["children"])
+    return maximum

+from unittest import TestCase

+            ("- first  \n  second\n", "- | first\n  | second\n"),
+            ("1. first\\\n   second\n", "1. | first\n   | second\n"),

+
+class TestMarkdownRendererRoundTrip(TestCase):
+    """Reformatting valid Markdown must not change its meaning: rendering the
+    reformatted source to HTML must match rendering the original source."""
+
+    to_html = create_markdown(escape=False)
+    reformat = create_markdown(renderer=MarkdownRenderer())
+
+    def assert_round_trip(self, text):
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self.to_html(self.reformat(text)),
+            self.to_html(text),
+        )
+
+    def test_escaped_block_markers(self):
+        # an escaped leading marker is literal text, not a new block
+        for marker in (r"\*", r"\-", r"\+", r"\#", r"\##", r"\>", r"1\.", r"3\)"):
+            self.assert_round_trip(marker + " literal\n")
+
+    def test_escaped_marker_on_continuation_line(self):
+        self.assert_round_trip("paragraph\n\\* not a list\n")
+
+    def test_escaped_marker_inside_list_item(self):
+        self.assert_round_trip("- item\n\n  \\# not a heading\n")
+
+    def test_escaped_backtick(self):
+        self.assert_round_trip(r"\`not code\`" + "\n")
+
+    def test_literal_inline_markers(self):
+        for text in (
+            r"\![label](https://example.com)" + "\n",
+            r"\\*emphasis*" + "\n",
+            r"\<b>text\</b>" + "\n",
+            r"\<https://example.com>" + "\n",
+            r"\©" + "\n",
+            r"\A" + "\n",
+            r"\A" + "\n",
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(text=text):
+                self.assert_round_trip(text)
+
+    def test_inline_punctuation_and_real_markup_controls(self):
+        for text in (
+            "Tom & Jerry!\n",
+            "Entities: © A A ¬anentity;\n",
+            "C# and a.b.c, (parentheses), [unmatched brackets]\n",
+            "*emphasis* and `code ©`\n",
+            "![image](https://example.com/image.png)\n",
+            "<b>real HTML</b>\n",
+            "<https://example.com/?a=1&b=2>\n",
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(text=text):
+                self.assert_round_trip(text)
+
+    def test_escaped_emphasis_markers(self):
+        # an escaped "*"/"_" is a literal delimiter, not emphasis; re-emitting
+        # it unescaped would turn plain text back into <em>/<strong>
+        for text in (
+            r"\*not emphasis\*" + "\n",
+            r"\_not emphasis\_" + "\n",
+            r"\*\*not strong\*\*" + "\n",
+            r"\_\_not strong\_\_" + "\n",
+            r"a word\_with\_underscores" + "\n",
+            r"2 \* 3 \* 4" + "\n",
+            r"trailing star\*" + "\n",
+            r"\*leading star" + "\n",

+            self.assert_round_trip(text)
+
+    def test_real_emphasis_not_over_escaped(self):

+        # spaces around a "*"/"_" must not gain stray backslashes

+            "**strong**\n",
+            "***both***\n",
+            "_under_ and __strong__\n",
+            "a *b* and _c_ mixed\n",
+            "2 * 3 = 6 and 4 * 5\n",

+
+    def test_codespan_containing_backticks(self):

+    def test_multiline_setext_heading(self):

+    def test_leading_blank_lines_preserved(self):

+    def test_markdown_list_content(self):

+import re
+from unittest import TestCase
+
+from mistune.core import InlineState
+from mistune.inline_parser import InlineParser
+from mistune.plugins.footnotes import INLINE_FOOTNOTE, parse_inline_footnote
+
+
+class _NoMembershipList(list[str]):
+    def __contains__(self, item: object) -> bool:
+        raise AssertionError("footnote membership must use footnote_indexes")
+
+
+class TestFootnoteSecurity(TestCase):
+    def test_inline_footnote_membership_uses_index_mapping(self):
+        notes = _NoMembershipList(["FIRST"])
+        indexes = {"FIRST": 0}
+        state = InlineState(
+            {
+                "ref_footnotes": {"FIRST": "First note", "SECOND": "Second note"},
+                "footnotes": notes,
+                "footnote_indexes": indexes,
+            }
+        )
+        match = re.match(INLINE_FOOTNOTE, "[^second]")
+        self.assertIsNotNone(match)
+        assert match is not None
+
+        parse_inline_footnote(InlineParser(), match, state)
+
+        self.assertEqual(notes, ["FIRST", "SECOND"])
+        self.assertEqual(indexes, {"FIRST": 0, "SECOND": 1})
+        self.assertEqual(
+            state.tokens,
+            [{"type": "footnote_ref", "raw": "SECOND", "attrs": {"index": 2}}],
+        )

+from unittest import TestCase
+
+from mistune import HTMLRenderer, create_markdown

+

+class TestImageDirectiveSecurity(TestCase):

+        md = create_markdown(escape=True, plugins=[FencedDirective([Image()])])
+        html = md("```{image} x.jpg\n:width: 100vw;height:100vh;position:fixed;top:0\n:height: 50%\n:alt: <alt>\n```\n")
+
+        self.assertIn('alt="<alt>"', html)
+        self.assertIn('style="height:50%;"', html)
+        self.assertNotIn("position:fixed", html)
+
+    def test_figure_directive_escapes_class_and_rejects_figwidth_css_injection(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=True, plugins=[FencedDirective([Figure()])])
+        html = md(
+            '```{figure} x.jpg\n:figclass: evil" onclick="alert(1)\n:figwidth: 10px;position:fixed\n\ncaption\n```\n'
+        )
+
+        self.assertIn('class="figure evil" onclick="alert(1)"', html)
+        self.assertNotIn('onclick="alert(1)"', html)
+        self.assertNotIn("position:fixed", html)
+        self.assertNotIn('style="width:', html)

+        self.assertIn('href="#harmful-link"', image)
+        self.assertIn('style="height:50%;"', image)
+        self.assertNotIn("position:fixed", image)
+        self.assertIn('class="figure wide" onclick="marker"', figure)
+        self.assertNotIn('onclick="marker"', figure)
+        self.assertNotIn("position:fixed", figure)

+import os
+import tempfile
+from unittest import TestCase
+
+from mistune import create_markdown
+from mistune.directives import Include, RSTDirective
+
+
+class TestIncludeSecurity(TestCase):
+    def test_include_rejects_traversal_and_absolute_paths(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
+            root = os.path.join(tmpdir, "root")
+            os.mkdir(root)
+            secret = os.path.join(tmpdir, "secret.txt")
+            source = os.path.join(root, "source.md")
+            with open(secret, "w") as f:
+                f.write("topsecret")
+            with open(source, "w") as f:
+                f.write(".. include:: ../secret.txt\n\n.. include:: " + secret + "\n")
+
+            md = create_markdown(plugins=[RSTDirective([Include()])])
+            html = md.read(source)[0]
+
+        self.assertIn("Could not include outside source dir", html)
+        self.assertNotIn("topsecret", html)
+
+    def test_include_text_escapes_with_html_escape_enabled(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
+            source = os.path.join(tmpdir, "source.md")
+            child = os.path.join(tmpdir, "child.txt")
+            with open(source, "w") as f:
+                f.write(".. include:: child.txt\n")
+            with open(child, "w") as f:
+                f.write("<script>alert(1)</script>")
+
+            md = create_markdown(plugins=[RSTDirective([Include()])])
+            html = md.read(source)[0]
+
+        self.assertIn("<script>alert(1)</script>", html)
+        self.assertNotIn("<script>", html)
+
+    def test_include_html_escapes_with_html_escape_enabled(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
+            source = os.path.join(tmpdir, "source.md")
+            child = os.path.join(tmpdir, "child.html")
+            with open(source, "w") as f:
+                f.write(".. include:: child.html\n")
+            with open(child, "w") as f:
+                f.write("<script>alert(1)</script>")
+
+            md = create_markdown(plugins=[RSTDirective([Include()])])
+            html = md.read(source)[0]
+
+        self.assertIn("<script>alert(1)</script>", html)
+        self.assertNotIn("<script>", html)
+
+    def test_include_rejects_circular_references(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
+            a = os.path.join(tmpdir, "a.md")

+        self.assertIn("Could not include circular reference", html)

+from unittest import TestCase
+
+from mistune import create_markdown
+from tests.perf_utils import assert_near_linear
+
+
+class TestInlineParserSecurity(TestCase):
+    def assert_max_token_depth(self, tokens, token_type, max_depth):
+        stack = [(token, 0) for token in tokens]
+        while stack:
+            token, depth = stack.pop()
+            if token["type"] == token_type:
+                depth += 1
+                self.assertLessEqual(depth, max_depth)
+            for child in token.get("children", ()):
+                stack.append((child, depth))
+
+    def test_link_title_redos_payload_returns_quickly(self):
+        md = create_markdown()
+
+        def render(size):
+            return md('[x](y "' + "\\!" * size + ")")
+
+        _small, html = assert_near_linear(self, render, 1000, 2000)
+        self.assertIn("[x](y", html)
+
+    def test_nested_bracket_link_input_does_not_recurse_forever(self):
+        md = create_markdown()
+
+        def render(size):
+            return md("[" * size + "x" + "]" * size)
+
+        _small, html = assert_near_linear(self, render, 4000, 8000)
+        self.assertIn("[", html)
+
+    def test_failed_outer_bracket_preserves_nested_link(self):

+        self.assertEqual('<p>[foo]<a href="https://example.com">bar</a></p>\n', html)
+
+    def test_unmatched_bracket_input_returns_quickly(self):
+        md = create_markdown()
+
+        def render(size):
+            return md("[" * size)
+
+        _small, html = assert_near_linear(self, render, 2000, 4000)
+        self.assertIn("[", html)
+
+    def test_deep_emphasis_input_does_not_recurse_forever(self):

+from unittest import TestCase

+class TestMathSecurity(TestCase):
+    def test_math_plugin_escapes_math_content(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=True, plugins=["math"])
+
+        inline_html = md("$<script>alert(1)</script>$\n")
+        block_html = md("$$\n<script>alert(1)</script>\n$$\n")

+        self.assertIn("<script>alert(1)</script>", inline_html)
+        self.assertIn("<script>alert(1)</script>", block_html)
+        self.assertNotIn("<script>", inline_html)
+        self.assertNotIn("<script>", block_html)
+
+    def test_math_plugin_escapes_content_when_raw_html_is_enabled(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=False, plugins=["math"])
+
+        self.assertIn("<marker>", md("$<marker>$\n"))
+
+    def test_repeated_inline_math_openers_are_near_linear(self):
+        md = create_markdown(plugins=["math"])
+
+        def render(size):
+            return md("$a " * size + "\n")
+

@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+from unittest import TestCase
+
+from mistune import create_markdown
+from mistune.directives import FencedDirective, TableOfContents
+from mistune.toc import add_toc_hook, render_toc_ul
+
+
+class TestTocSecurity(TestCase):
+    def test_custom_heading_id_is_escaped(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=True)
+        add_toc_hook(md, heading_id=lambda token, index: token.get("text", ""))
+
+        html, _state = md.parse('## foo" onmouseover="alert(1)" x="\n')
+
+        self.assertIn('id="foo" onmouseover="alert(1)" x=""', html)
+        self.assertNotIn('onmouseover="alert(1)"', html)
+
+    def test_toc_href_is_escaped(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=True)
+        add_toc_hook(md, heading_id=lambda token, index: token.get("text", ""))
+
+        _html, state = md.parse('## x"><script>alert(1)</script><a href="\n')
+        toc = render_toc_ul(state.env["toc_items"])
+
+        self.assertIn('href="#x"><script>alert(1)</script><a href=""', toc)
+        self.assertNotIn("<script>", toc)
+
+    def test_default_toc_id_avoids_existing_html_id_collision(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=False)
+        add_toc_hook(md)
+
+        html, state = md.parse('<div id="toc_1"></div>\n\n# title\n')
+        toc = render_toc_ul(state.env["toc_items"])
+
+        self.assertIn('<h1 id="toc_1_1">title</h1>', html)
+        self.assertIn('href="#toc_1_1"', toc)
+
+    def test_directive_toc_avoids_sequential_html_id_collisions(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=False, plugins=[FencedDirective([TableOfContents()])])
+        source = '<div id="toc_1"></div>\n<div id="toc_1_1"></div>\n\n```{toc}\n```\n\n# title\n'
+
+        html = md(source)
+
+        self.assertIn('<h1 id="toc_1_2">title</h1>', html)
+        self.assertIn('href="#toc_1_2"', html)
+
+    def test_toc_hooks_preserve_existing_heading_id(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=False, plugins=[FencedDirective([TableOfContents()])])
+
+        def set_heading_id(_md, state):
+            for token in state.tokens:
+                if token["type"] == "heading":
+                    token["attrs"]["id"] = "existing"
+
+        md.before_render_hooks.insert(0, set_heading_id)
+        html = md("```{toc}\n```\n\n# title\n")
+
+        self.assertIn('<h1 id="existing">title</h1>', html)
+        self.assertIn('href="#existing"', html)
+        self.assertNotIn('id="toc_1"', html)
+
+    def test_two_toc_sections_share_heading_ids(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=False, plugins=[FencedDirective([TableOfContents()])])
+        html = md("```{toc}\n```\n\n```{toc}\n```\n\n# title\n")
+
+        self.assertEqual(html.count('<h1 id="toc_1">title</h1>'), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(html.count('href="#toc_1"'), 2)
+
+    def test_hook_preserves_existing_heading_id(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=False)
+
+        def set_heading_id(_md, state):
+            for token in state.tokens:
+                if token["type"] == "heading":
+                    token["attrs"]["id"] = "existing"
+
+        md.before_render_hooks.append(set_heading_id)
+        add_toc_hook(md)
+        html, state = md.parse("# title\n")
+
+        self.assertIn('<h1 id="existing">title</h1>', html)
+        self.assertIn('href="#existing"', render_toc_ul(state.env["toc_items"]))

@@ -0,0 +1,83 @@
+from unittest import TestCase
+
+from mistune import create_markdown, html
+
+
+class TestSafeUrlSecurity(TestCase):
+    def test_known_harmful_url_schemes_are_blocked(self):
+        for url in [
+            "javascript:alert(1)",
+            "vbscript:msgbox(1)",
+            "file:///etc/passwd",
+            "data:text/html;base64,PHNjcmlwdD4=",
+            "feed:javascript:alert(1)",
+            "livescript:alert(1)",
+            "mocha:alert(1)",
+            "view-source:javascript:alert(1)",
+            "jar:javascript:alert(1)",
+            "ms-its:javascript:alert(1)",
+            "mk:@MSITStore:javascript:alert(1)",
+            "res:javascript:",
+        ]:
+            rendered = html(f"[h]({url})")
+            self.assertIn('href="#harmful-link"', rendered, url)
+
+    def test_unknown_url_scheme_is_blocked(self):
+        rendered = html("[h](x-javascript:alert(1))")
+
+        self.assertIn('href="#harmful-link"', rendered)
+
+    def test_reference_and_autolink_harmful_url_schemes_are_blocked(self):
+        cases = [
+            "[h][r]\n\n[r]: feed:javascript:alert(1)",
+            "<feed:javascript:alert(1)>",
+            "[h][r]\n\n[r]: x-javascript:alert(1)",
+            "<x-javascript:alert(1)>",
+        ]
+        for text in cases:
+            rendered = create_markdown()(text)
+            self.assertIn('href="#harmful-link"', rendered, text)
+
+    def test_percent_encoded_harmful_url_scheme_is_blocked(self):
+        for text in [
+            "[h](javascript%3Aalert(1))",
+            "[h](javascript%253Aalert(1))",
+            "[h][r]\n\n[r]: javascript%3Aalert(1)",
+            "![h](data%3Atext/html;base64,PHNjcmlwdD4=)",
+            "[h](view-source:javascript:alert(1))",
+            "[h](%20javascript%3Aalert(1))",
+        ]:
+            rendered = create_markdown()(text)
+            self.assertIn("#harmful-link", rendered, text)
+
+    def test_safe_percent_encoded_data_image_is_allowed(self):
+        rendered = create_markdown()("![h](data%3Aimage/png;base64,AAAA)")
+        self.assertIn('src="data%3Aimage/png;base64,AAAA"', rendered)
+
+    def test_safe_url_schemes_are_allowed(self):
+        for url in [
+            "http://example.com",
+            "https://example.com",
+            "mailto:user@example.com",
+            "tel:+123456789",
+            "ftp://example.com/file",
+            "ftps://example.com/file",
+            "irc://example.com/channel",
+            "ircs://example.com/channel",
+            "//example.com/path",
+            "/path",
+            "./path:with-colon",
+            "../path:with-colon",
+            "path/with:colon",
+            "#fragment",
+            "?query",
+        ]:
+            rendered = html(f"[h]({url})")
+            self.assertIn(f'href="{url}"', rendered, url)
+
+    def test_attribute_escaping_is_independent_of_raw_html_mode(self):
+        md = create_markdown(escape=False)
+        rendered = md('![a"<b>](https://example.com/image.png "t\\\"itle")')
+
+        self.assertIn('alt="a""', rendered)
+        self.assertIn('title="t"itle"', rendered)

index 0000000..1dd228f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/autose.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,256 @@
+# AutoSE: issue in, reviewed pull request out.
+# Trigger: label an issue `autose`, comment `/autose` on an issue, or `/autose review` on an open PR
+# (trusted users only). A human always makes the merge decision; this workflow never merges.
+name: autose
+
+on:
+  issues:
+    types: [labeled]
+  issue_comment:
+    types: [created]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      issue: { description: "Issue number (build mode)", required: false, default: "" }
+      pr: { description: "PR number (review mode)", required: false, default: "" }
+      mode: { description: "build | review", required: false, default: "build" }
+      variant: { description: "config variant (baseline | no_arch | weak_reviewer)", required: false, default: "baseline" }
+      stop_after: { description: "'' | spec | design | test (experiments)", required: false, default: "" }
+
+permissions: {}  # nothing by default; every job opts in to the minimum it needs
+
+# One run at a time per issue/PR; a second trigger queues instead of racing on the same branch.
+# Comments that are not /autose commands get a unique group so they never displace a queued run.
+concurrency:
+  group: >-
+    ${{ ((github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/autose'))
+        || (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.label.name == 'autose')
+        || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
+        && format('autose-{0}', github.event.issue.number || inputs.pr || inputs.issue)
+        || format('autose-noop-{0}', github.run_id) }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+env:
+  GEMINI_CLI_VERSION: "0.70.0"
+
+jobs:
+  gate:
+    if: >-
+      (github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.label.name == 'autose') ||
+      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/autose')) ||
+      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions: { issues: write, pull-requests: write }
+    outputs:
+      mode: ${{ steps.g.outputs.mode }}
+      issue: ${{ steps.g.outputs.issue }}
+      pr: ${{ steps.g.outputs.pr }}
+      variant: ${{ steps.g.outputs.variant }}
+      stop_after: ${{ steps.g.outputs.stop_after }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with: { path: tool, persist-credentials: false, sparse-checkout: autose }
+      - id: g
+        run: python3 tool/autose/gate.py
+        env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}", GH_REPO: "${{ github.repository }}" }
+
+  build:  # LangGraph build graph: stages 1-5 (agents + parallel test workers + code checks + release)
+    needs: gate
+    if: needs.gate.outputs.mode == 'build'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 90
+    permissions: { contents: write, pull-requests: write, issues: write, actions: write }
+    outputs:
+      pr: ${{ steps.orch.outputs.pr }}
+      branch: ${{ steps.orch.outputs.branch }}
+      status: ${{ steps.orch.outputs.status }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7  # tooling always from the default branch
+        with: { path: tool, persist-credentials: false }
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7  # the repository the agents work in
+        with: { path: work, fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false }
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.0
+        with: { python-version: "3.13" }
+      - run: npm install -g "@google/gemini-cli@${GEMINI_CLI_VERSION}"
+      - name: AutoSE tool environment (LangGraph)
+        run: uv venv -q "$RUNNER_TEMP/autose-venv" && uv pip install -q --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/autose-venv/bin/python" -r tool/autose/requirements.txt
+      - run: uv sync --group test
+        working-directory: work
+      - name: Previous attempt's checkpoint (only exists when this job is re-run)
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v7
+        continue-on-error: true
+        with: { name: build, path: out }
+      - id: orch
+        working-directory: work
+        run: |
+          "$RUNNER_TEMP/autose-venv/bin/python" ../tool/autose/run.py build --issue "$ISSUE" --variant "$VARIANT" --stop-after "$STOP_AFTER" --repo . --out ../out
+        env:
+          ISSUE: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue }}
+          VARIANT: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.variant }}
+          STOP_AFTER: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.stop_after }}
+          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  # used only by the orchestrator; stripped from agent processes
+          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6
+        if: always()
+        with: { name: build, path: out/, include-hidden-files: true, overwrite: true }
+
+  review-1:  # independent reviewer: read-only token, own model/prompt, no builder artifacts
+    needs: [gate, build]
+    if: >-
+      always() && needs.gate.result == 'success' &&

+      - run: uv sync --group test

+++ b/ARCHITECTURE.md
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+# Mistune: Architecture
+
+Mistune is a fast, pure-Python Markdown parser (CommonMark 0.31.2 compatible) with pluggable
+renderers, syntax plugins and directives. This document describes the main components, the key
+design decisions behind them, and the rules a developer should not break when changing the code.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Component overview
+
+| # | Component | Files | What it does |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | **Public API / orchestrator** | `__init__.py`, `markdown.py` | `create_markdown()` builds a `Markdown` instance from a renderer name or instance and a list of plugins (by name or callable). `Markdown.parse()` runs the pipeline: block parse, then inline parse, then render, with hook lists in between. |
+| 2 | **Core abstractions** | `core.py` | `BlockState` / `InlineState` (source, cursor, tokens, a shared `env` dict), the generic `Parser` (named-regex rule registry plus a compiled scanner) and `BaseRenderer` (dispatch by token type). Everything else builds on these. |
+| 3 | **Block parser** | `block_parser.py`, `list_parser.py` | Turns the document into block tokens: headings, code, quotes, lists, HTML, reference-link definitions, paragraphs. Leaves inline text unparsed in a `"text"` key. |
+| 4 | **Inline parser** | `inline_parser.py`, `_inline/` | Parses inline text into tokens: escapes, code spans, emphasis, links, autolinks, inline HTML, breaks. `_inline/delimiters.py` (`DelimiterScanner`) finds closing markers, and `_inline/emphasis.py` and `_inline/links.py` hold the CommonMark algorithms. |
+| 5 | **Renderers** | `renderers/html.py`, `markdown.py`, `rst.py` | Turn the token tree into output. `HTMLRenderer` (`NAME="html"`) also owns output safety (escaping, URL protocol policy). `MarkdownRenderer` (`"markdown"`) and `RSTRenderer` (`"rst"`) convert tokens back to text formats. |
+| 6 | **Plugins** | `plugins/` | Optional syntax extensions (table, footnotes, strikethrough, mark, insert, superscript, subscript, math, abbr, def_list, ruby, spoiler, task_lists, url). Each is a callable `plugin(md)` that registers parse rules, render functions and hooks. |
+| 7 | **Directives** | `directives/` | A generic block-extension framework. Syntax front-ends (`RSTDirective`, `FencedDirective`) host syntax-independent directive plugins (`Admonition`, `TableOfContents`, `Include`, `Image`, `Figure`). |
+| 8 | **Utilities** | `util.py`, `helpers.py`, `toc.py` | Escaping (`escape`, `escape_url`, `safe_entity`), label normalisation (`unikey`), shared regex fragments and link parsing helpers, and TOC hook helpers. |
+
+### Who calls whom
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    U([user code]) --> API["create_markdown() / Markdown<br/>(__init__.py, markdown.py)"]
+    API -->|"1. parse(state)"| BP["BlockParser<br/>(block_parser, list_parser)"]
+    API -->|"2. inline(text, env)<br/>per text token"| IP["InlineParser<br/>(inline_parser, _inline/)"]
+    API -->|"3. renderer(tokens, state)"| R["Renderers<br/>html / markdown / rst"]
+    API -->|"plugin(md) at construction"| PL["Plugins<br/>(plugins/)"]
+    API -->|"plugin(md) at construction"| DI["Directives<br/>(directives/)"]
+    PL -.->|"register rules"| BP
+    PL -.->|"register rules"| IP
+    PL -.->|"register render fns,<br/>append hooks"| R
+    DI -.->|"register one block rule"| BP
+    DI -.->|"register render fns"| R
+    BP --> CORE["core.py<br/>Parser, BlockState, InlineState, BaseRenderer"]
+    IP --> CORE
+    R --> CORE
+    BP --> UT["util.py / helpers.py"]
+    IP --> UT
+    R --> UT
+```
+
+Solid arrows are calls made on every `parse()`. Dotted arrows are registrations that happen once, when
+the `Markdown` instance is built.
+
+**Pipeline in order** (`Markdown.parse`, `markdown.py:71-102`): normalise newlines → `before_parse_hooks` →
+`BlockParser.parse(state)` → `before_render_hooks` → `render_state()` (this runs the inline parser on each
+token that still has `"text"`, then calls the renderer) → `after_render_hooks`. Hooks that run before
+rendering therefore see block tokens whose inline text is not parsed yet. With `renderer="ast"` the
+renderer is `None` and the token list itself is returned.
+
+**Tokens** are plain dicts: `type` (required; selects the render method), `children`, `text` (unparsed
+inline text), `raw` (literal text), and `attrs` (passed to HTML render functions as keyword arguments).
+`state.env` is shared by all nested block and inline states of one document. Multi-pass features such as
+reference links, footnotes and TOC keep their data there.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Architecture Decision Records
+
+### ADR-1: A token AST is the only interface between parsing and rendering
+**Status:** Verified. Evidence: upstream commit `a728952` "fix(plugin): fix footnote plugins when rendering ast";
+code comments `__init__.py:49` ("explicit and more similar to 2.x's API", for `renderer="ast"`),
+`renderers/html.py:91` ("backward compitable with v2") and `directives/toc.py:88` ("only works with HTML renderer").
+
+* **Context:** Mistune serves several output formats (HTML, Markdown, reStructuredText, raw AST for tooling),
+  and third-party plugins must keep working whichever format is chosen.
+* **Decision:** Parsers only produce a tree of dict tokens, and renderers only consume it. A renderer is selected
+  per instance (`renderer=` in `create_markdown`). `renderer=None` / `"ast"` returns the tree. Each renderer
+  declares a `NAME`, and extensions register render functions only for the renderer names they support.
+* **Alternatives considered:** (a) parsers emit HTML directly (simplest and fastest, but one format only); (b) a
+  typed node-class hierarchy instead of dicts (stricter, but heavier and harder for plugins to extend).
+* **Consequences:** New output formats need only a new renderer. Plugin parsing works for every renderer, but
+  output support is per renderer, so a token type without a render function raises `AttributeError` at render
+  time (`core.py:274-280`). Several plugins and directives (e.g. TOC) are HTML-only. Dict tokens are untyped,
+  so token shape is a convention rather than something the type checker enforces.
+
+### ADR-2: Directives separate syntax (front-ends) from semantics (directive plugins)
+**Status:** Verified. Evidence: upstream commit `edb9f0c` (2022-10-31) "Refactor directive to support more styles",
+which introduced `DirectivePlugin`; follow-ups `1d54bc4` "Update fenced directive to support other markers",
+`465040e` "Use directive-type instead of directive-name", `dab16f1` "Rename RstDirective to RSTDirective"
+(the deprecated alias is still in `directives/__init__.py:12`).
+
+* **Context:** Users want block extensions (admonitions, TOC, includes, figures) in more than one syntax: the
+  reStructuredText style `.. name:: title` and the MyST-like fenced style ```` ```{name} title ````.
+* **Decision:** A `BaseDirective` front-end (`RSTDirective`, `FencedDirective`) owns the syntax. It registers
+  one block rule and dispatches by directive *type* to handlers. A `DirectivePlugin` owns the meaning and reads
+  type, title, options and content only through `self.parse_*` helpers, which delegate to whichever
+  front-end's `DirectiveParser` it was attached to (`directives/_base.py:118-121`).
+* **Alternatives considered:** (a) one block plugin per directive per syntax (duplicated logic); (b) supporting only
+  one syntax.
+* **Consequences:** A single directive class works under both syntaxes unchanged, and adding a new syntax means
+  writing a new front-end. Unknown directive types render as `block_error` tokens instead of failing
+  (`directives/_base.py:91-97`). Directive bodies are parsed as nested block content with the parent's rules,
+  bounded by `max_nested_level`.
+
+### ADR-3: Extension by registering named regex rules into an ordered rule list
+**Status:** Inferred. Reasoned from `core.py:181-255`. The mechanism is documented in code (the `register` docstring
+says it "is usually used to create a new plugin"), but I found no commit or issue that states why this design
+was chosen over the alternatives. One related, verified consequence: `plugins/speedup.py:10-15` says the former
+speed-up plugin is now a no-op because "the paragraph and inline text fast paths are now part of the core
+parsers" (commit `5de41fb`).
+
+* **Context:** The parser must be fast in pure Python and extensible by third parties without forking.
+* **Decision:** Each parser keeps `specification` (rule name → regex), an ordered `rules` list and `_methods`.
+  `compile_sc()` joins the active rules into one alternation of named groups (cached), and a match is dispatched
+  by `m.lastgroup`. Extensions call `register(name, pattern, func, before=...)` on an existing instance; they
+  do not subclass the parser.
+* **Alternatives considered:** (a) subclassing parsers per feature (does not compose across plugins); (b) a formal
+  grammar or PEG parser (cleaner, slower, harder to extend at runtime); (c) a character-by-character
+  hand-written state machine (fast, but hard to extend).
+* **Consequences:** Plugins compose freely, and priority is controlled by order: earlier alternatives win, so
+  `before="link"` etc. matters. If `before` names a rule that is not present, the new rule is appended
+  (`core.py:240-248`). A parse function signals "not a match" by returning `None`: the inline parser then
+  consumes one character as text (`inline_parser.py:307-312`), and the block parser turns the line into
+  paragraph text (`block_parser.py:471-478`).
+
+---
+
+## 3. Constraints (do not break these)
+
+| # | Constraint | Where it can be seen |
+|---|---|---|
+| C1 | **The core and parser layers must not import renderers, plugins or directives.** `core.py`, `block_parser.py`, `inline_parser.py`, `list_parser.py`, `helpers.py`, `util.py` and `_inline/` only import each other. Only `markdown.py` imports from `plugins` (the `Plugin` protocol, for typing). Extensions depend on the core, never the reverse. | `core.py:1-23`, `block_parser.py:6-18`, `inline_parser.py:6-10`, `markdown.py:3-6` |
+| C2 | **Plugins and directives import `Markdown`, the parser classes and renderer classes only under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`.** `markdown.py` imports `plugins`, so a runtime import back would be circular. Runtime imports from plugins and directives are limited to `core`, `util`, `helpers` and sibling modules. | `plugins/formatting.py:5-8`, `plugins/math.py:3-8`, `directives/_base.py:5-8` |
+| C3 | **Register render functions only for renderers you support, and guard for "no renderer".** `md.renderer` is `None` in AST mode (`__init__.py:50`), so the pattern is `if md.renderer and md.renderer.NAME == "html": md.renderer.register(...)`. Parse rules are registered unconditionally so the AST is the same for every output format. *Known exception:* `Admonition` instead does `assert md.renderer is not None` (`directives/admonition.py:57`), so it fails with `renderer="ast"`. Do not copy that pattern. | `plugins/formatting.py:111-112`, `directives/toc.py:87-91` |
+| C4 | **Directive plugins subclass `DirectivePlugin`, register handlers with `directive.register(type, fn)`, and read syntax only through `self.parse_type / parse_title / parse_options / parse_content / parse_tokens`.** They must not parse RST or fenced syntax themselves or modify a front-end, otherwise they stop working under the other front-end. | `directives/_base.py:124-150`, `directives/admonition.py:25-61` |
+| C5 | **Every token type a parser emits must have a render method or a registered render function in each renderer that will see it.** `BaseRenderer._get_method` raises `AttributeError('No renderer ...')` otherwise. HTML render functions receive the rendered children (or `raw`) positionally and `attrs` as keyword arguments, and must escape any text they insert themselves (`util.escape` / `safe_entity`). | `core.py:274-285`, `renderers/html.py:90-107`, `util.py:23-47` |
+
+---
+
+## 4. Conventions and testing
+
+* Parse functions are `parse_<rule>(parser, m, state) -> Optional[int]` (they return the new position) and render
+  functions are `render_<token>(renderer, text, **attrs) -> str`. A built-in plugin is exposed by name through the
+  `_plugins` registry (`plugins/__init__.py:7`), and a built-in directive is exported from `directives/__init__.py`.
+* Code is fully type-hinted and checked with `mypy --strict` over `src/mistune`. Linting is `ruff` (rules `I`, `F`, line
+  length 120).
+* Tests: `python -m pytest` (`pythonpath = ["src", "."]`, warnings are errors). Most syntax tests are data-driven
+  fixtures in `tests/fixtures/*.txt`. Each `example` block holds Markdown input, a line containing only `.`, and the
+  expected HTML, loaded through `tests/__init__.py`. Plugin fixtures are run with and without `speedup`
+  (`tests/test_plugins.py`).

+> [!NOTE]
+>
+> I’ve released [Wenmode](https://github.com/lepture/wenmode), a new Markdown parser inspired by the lessons learned from Mistune.
+>
+> Wenmode focuses on fast CommonMark-style parsing, explicit rule composition, mdast-compatible AST output, safe HTML defaults, streaming output, and pluggable renderers.
+>
+> In the current benchmark suite, Wenmode’s core Markdown-to-HTML path is about 1.5-1.8x as fast as Mistune across the tested documentation corpora. See the [benchmark results](https://wenmode.lepture.com/benchmarks/) for the exact setup and numbers.

+## Install
+
+To install mistune:
+
+```

+```

+## Overview
+
+Convert Markdown to HTML with ease:
+
+```python
+import mistune
+
+markdown = mistune.create_markdown()
+markdown(your_markdown_text)
+```
+
+`create_markdown()` escapes raw HTML by default. For compatibility,
+`mistune.html(trusted_markdown_text)` enables raw HTML and several plugins; use
+that legacy helper only for trusted input or sanitize its output externally.
